headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-edit risks between LangGraph and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest application-defined files and has no self-isolation, while Mentat reads files passed on the command line and writes diffs. If Mentat-generated content is fed into LangGraph state or files, instructions can be smuggled across the shared workspace. The pathway is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Mentat output is written into files that LangGraph later reads as state or prompts
IF the orchestrator passes shared workspace artifacts between the two agents without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Add a provenance header to every file passed between agents
Require manual review before LangGraph consumes Mentat output
Disable automatic ingestion of workspace files where possible

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write filesystem content, and both have broad network egress to model providers. LangGraph touches application-defined graph state and Mentat touches selected source files, so a shared workspace can expose code or state to both backends. This is a default-config risk in a pairwise setup, not merely an unusual edge case.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or checkout
IF either agent forwards file contents or state to its model provider during normal operation
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Restrict each agent to least-privilege file paths
Redact secrets before either agent reads shared files
Turn off network access for one agent during sensitive tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state. Their concurrency models both allow multiple instances, and Mentat shares state via filesystem. Without explicit locking, concurrent edits or git mutations can collide in the same repo or workspace.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF Mentat modifies git state while LangGraph or its nodes also write files concurrently
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Assign separate branches or worktrees
Disable concurrent runs against the same repo
Have one agent produce patches only, then apply them sequentially

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can pass outputs between nodes, and Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals. If LangGraph treats Mentat output as authoritative without verification, a mistaken or malicious proposal can cascade into multi-file edits or downstream actions. The pair creates a clear handoff path, though not an irreversible default harm.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes Mentat proposals into later nodes without validation
IF downstream nodes apply edits or actions based on Mentat output
mitigations: Insert a validation step before applying any proposal
Require human approval for multi-file diffs
Compare proposed edits against tests or lint checks
Log and diff every handoff between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly mention model-provider API keys plus code or graph state, so no specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. The main compliance concern is generic retention/logging of workspace content, which is possible but not evidenced as a default breach. The other agent is cited because the pairwise workspace and provider flow are the relevant context.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace or prompts
IF the configured model provider retains prompts or files beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts and files
Review provider retention settings before use
Use a local model for sensitive tasks
Document data handling boundaries for both agents
